**(C)** Viroid

T. O. Diener (1971) found that potato spindle tuber disease is caused by a low molecular weight, single stranded RNA that lacks a protein coat; these infectious RNA strands are called viroids. Every virus, whether a bacteriophage, a plant virus or an animal virus, has a protein coat (capsid) around its nucleic acid, and a bacteriophage normally carries double stranded DNA, not RNA.

**(A)** Dinoflagellate

The chapter names *Gonyaulax*, a dinoflagellate, as responsible for the famous red tide that makes even the sea appear red; dinoflagellates carry red and other pigments and can multiply rapidly in the sea. Euglenoids are mostly freshwater, chrysophytes are the diatoms and golden algae, and a lichen is an alga living with a fungus, not a marine bloom.

**(D)** Cyanobacteria

Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae such as *Nostoc*) carry chlorophyll a and other pigments and make their own food by photosynthesis, so they are autotrophs. The chapter lists the other groups among bacteria that do not photosynthesise: *Lactobacilli* curdle milk, nitrogen-fixing *Azotobacter* is heterotrophic, and methanogens live in the gut of ruminants and produce methane.

[Note: the chapter does not state the nutrition of methanogens; standard biology gives that many methanogens are archaebacteria that use carbon dioxide, so the question works only because cyanobacteria are the one clearly photosynthetic group.]

**(D)** Sporozoan

*Paramoecium* moves by cilia, so it is a ciliated protist. *Plasmodium*, the malaria parasite, has no locomotory organ and forms spores in one stage of its life cycle, so the chapter calls it a sporozoan protozoan. Amoeboid protozoans move by pseudopodia (*Amoeba*), flagellate protozoans by flagella (*Trypanosoma*), and Ciliophora is the ciliate group to which *Paramoecium* itself belongs.
